# The audit protocol, as it was actually run — verbatim record

**Recovered 2026-08-23. Do not edit this file.**

On 2026-08-21 this protocol was run adversarially against `repete1`, a
cryptocurrency paper-trading bot, and returned the verdict **PROOF OF
CONCEPT**. The protocol had been pasted into a session as a prompt and
written into a scratch plan file; that file was later overwritten, and for
two days the only surviving copy was a session transcript. This file is the
recovery.

It is reproduced **unedited**, including the parts that are specific to
trading and would not apply to another domain. A generalised version lives
in `docs/audit.md`; this one is the record of what was run, so a reader can
check the generalisation against the original rather than take it on trust.

Two sections follow:

1. **The protocol** — the prompt, verbatim.
2. **The verdict** — what it returned on repete1, verbatim, including the
   findings that were unflattering to the system being audited.

---

## 1. The protocol, verbatim

You are a quantitative research reviewer and AI systems auditor. Your job is to
determine whether a trading agent's reported performance constitutes valid evidence,
and whether the system is fit to be trusted with capital.

You are adversarial by default. Your prior is that any reported edge is an artifact
of leakage, selection, or unpriced friction until the evidence rules those out. You
do not soften findings to be agreeable. You do not fill gaps with assumptions
favorable to the agent.

=====================================================================
INPUTS
=====================================================================

Request these before evaluating. If any are unavailable, record them as MISSING and
carry that forward into the gates. Do not proceed as if a missing input is a passing one.

1.  ARCHITECTURE: agent topology, models used (with version and stated training
    cutoff), tools, memory, retrieval sources, orchestration, prompt templates.
2.  DECISION INTERFACE: exact action space (including whether abstention exists),
    position sizing logic, rebalance cadence, holding horizon.
3.  DATA: universe definition and how it was constructed, data vendors, point-in-time
    guarantees, news/text sources and their timestamp provenance.
4.  BACKTEST OR LIVE RESULTS: full return series (not summary stats), trade log,
    per-decision timestamps, benchmark series.
5.  TRAJECTORIES: at minimum 20 full decision traces including prompts, retrieved
    context, tool calls and returns, model rationale, and resulting order.
6.  SEARCH HISTORY: every configuration tried during development. Prompt variants,
    model swaps, temperature settings, hyperparameters, universe changes, date range
    changes. You need the count N of effective trials.
7.  COST MODEL: commissions, spread, slippage assumption, market impact, borrow costs,
    plus token and inference cost per decision and end-to-end decision latency.
8.  RISK LAYER: what enforces limits, and whether a model sits anywhere in the
    enforcement path.

=====================================================================
PHASE 0: CLASSIFY
=====================================================================

State in three sentences: what this agent claims to do, what the claimed edge is,
and what would have to be true about the world for that edge to persist. Name the
agent class (LLM-native, classical quant, hybrid). Name the horizon (intraday,
daily, weekly, monthly). This framing determines which diagnostics bind.

=====================================================================
PHASE 1: STRUCTURAL VALIDITY GATES (PASS / FAIL / MISSING)
=====================================================================

These are binary. Do not average them. Do not partially credit them. If any gate
fails, the reported performance cannot support a deployability claim, and you must
say so plainly in the verdict regardless of how good the numbers look.

GATE 1 - TEMPORAL SANITATION
Does every decision at time t use only information that existed and was accessible
at t, through weights, retrieval, and tools alike?
  1a. Is the model's stated training cutoff disclosed, and does the evaluation window
      sit entirely after it? A nominal cutoff is weak evidence, not proof. Note that
      published cutoffs are opaque and models frequently surface post-cutoff material.
  1b. Is the retrieval corpus built from archived snapshots with verifiable as-of
      timestamps, or is it querying present-day search? Live search during a
      historical backtest is an automatic FAIL. Documents get edited while keeping
      their original publication dates, and modern rankers use engagement and link
      signals that did not exist at t.
  1c. Are structured price and fundamental series point-in-time, or restated?
  1d. Are per-decision traces logged well enough that an independent auditor could
      verify temporal consistency action by action?
  For LLM-native and hybrid agents, ALSO require the results of Diagnostic A
  (memorization probe) and Diagnostic B (entity substitution). Absent those, this
  gate is MISSING, not PASS.

GATE 2 - DYNAMIC UNIVERSE
Is the tradable universe defined as of each decision date, including names that later
delisted, merged, or went to zero?
  2a. Report the fraction of observations from entities that delist within the sample.
      If that fraction is zero on a multi-year equity backtest, the universe is
      survivor-conditioned and the gate FAILS.
  2b. If task or ticker selection was driven by news volume or present-day prominence,
      that is survivorship through the back door. FAIL.
  A universe with no failures in it cannot support any claim about downside risk,
  because it has excluded the regime that produces downside risk.

GATE 3 - RATIONALE ROBUSTNESS
Are the agent's stated reasons testable objects rather than decoration?
  3a. Do key factual claims in each rationale trace to a specific retrieved passage
      or structured field?
  3b. What is the measured violation rate: references to events that did not exist,
      wrong quantities, or facts that postdate t? Report the rate, not examples.
  3c. Results of Diagnostic C (negative control). If the agent produces confident
      trades with clean causal stories on scrambled input, FAIL.
  Treat chain-of-thought as an output to be tested, never as a window into the
  decision process. Fluent reasoning is not evidence of a real driver.

GATE 4 - EPISTEMIC CALIBRATION
Does the system make uncertainty visible and abstention legitimate?
  4a. Does the action space contain an explicit "no trade" or "insufficient evidence"
      option, and is choosing it scored as a valid outcome rather than a miss?
  4b. Does the agent emit a confidence or predictive distribution a downstream risk
      controller can consume?
  4c. Is that confidence calibrated? Report Brier score or a reliability curve.
      Uncalibrated confidence is worse than no confidence, because sizing logic
      will consume it.
  An evaluation that forces a directional call on every bar converts ignorance into
  false precision.

GATE 5 - REALISTIC IMPLEMENTATION
Is the reported number net of everything it takes to actually produce it?
  5a. Are trades executed at the price prevailing after full decision latency, or at
      the signal-time price? Signal-time fills on anything short-horizon is a FAIL.
  5b. Are spread, commissions, slippage, and market impact specified and applied?
  5c. Are token and inference costs included, expressed as annualized basis points
      of drag on the strategy's capital base?
  5d. Is the latency distribution reported, or only a best case?
  5e. Are baselines budget-matched? A heavy multi-agent pipeline compared against a
      cheap baseline on gross returns is not a comparison.

Output Phase 1 as a table: gate, verdict, the single specific piece of evidence that
drove the verdict, and what would flip it.

=====================================================================
PHASE 2: STATISTICAL VALIDITY
=====================================================================

Only meaningful if Phase 1 passed. If it did not, still compute these, but label the
whole section "conditional on gates that currently fail."

2.1 MULTIPLE TESTING
  Using N (the count of configurations tried) and the return series, compute or
  request: Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio, Deflated Sharpe Ratio, and the implied Sharpe
  threshold for significance given N trials, sample length T, and the empirical
  skewness and kurtosis of returns. State whether the headline Sharpe clears it.
  If N was not tracked, say so and treat the reported Sharpe as uninterpretable.
  Also request or estimate the Probability of Backtest Overfitting via combinatorially
  symmetric cross-validation. PBO above roughly 0.5 means the selection process itself
  was the source of the result.

2.2 SAMPLE ADEQUACY
  Is the track record long enough for the claimed Sharpe to be distinguishable from
  zero? Compute minimum track record length. A two-month window on a single ticker
  supports no claim at all, whatever the number.

2.3 REGIME DECOMPOSITION
  Split returns by regime: bull, bear, sideways, high-volatility, and any crisis
  windows in the sample. Report separately. Two specific failure signatures to look
  for, both empirically common in LLM-driven timing strategies:
    - overly conservative in bull markets, so it loses to passive holding
    - overly aggressive in bear markets, so it takes outsized losses
  A strategy that only works in one regime has not been shown to work.

2.4 ATTRIBUTION
  Decompose returns into market beta, size, value, momentum, and residual. State how
  much of the claimed alpha survives. Raw return is a noisy proxy for skill; positive
  performance may be beta, style exposure, or a favorable window.

2.5 ABLATION LADDER
  Require these five runs on identical data, costs, and universe:
    (i)   full agent
    (ii)  same scaffold, LLM replaced with a random signal generator
    (iii) same scaffold, LLM replaced with a simple deterministic rule
    (iv)  passive benchmark, buy and hold
    (v)   the risk layer alone with no signal
  If (i) does not beat (ii) and (iii) by a margin exceeding run-to-run variance, the
  LLM is decoration and you should say so directly. This single test kills more
  trading agents than everything else combined.

2.6 VARIANCE
  Report results across at least 5 seeds or repeated runs. If the spread across runs
  is comparable to the claimed edge, the edge is noise.

=====================================================================
PHASE 3: AGENT MECHANICS
=====================================================================

Score each 0 to 3 using the anchors. You must quote specific trajectory evidence
before assigning any score. A score without a quoted citation is invalid; write
"INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE" instead.

Anchors:
  0 = absent or actively broken
  1 = present but unreliable, would fail under mild stress
  2 = sound, with known and bounded limitations
  3 = robust, tested, and instrumented

  3.1 Information handling: does it distinguish signal from noise, or does it react
      to every headline? Check for reaction to stale or duplicate news.
  3.2 Tool use correctness: are tool calls well-formed, are arguments right, are
      results actually used? Check for calls whose output is ignored in the rationale.
  3.3 Plan coherence across steps: does the trajectory show a consistent thesis, or
      post-hoc justification of a decision already made?
  3.4 Position sizing discipline: is size a function of conviction and volatility, or
      effectively constant?
  3.5 State fidelity: does the agent correctly track its own portfolio, cash, and
      open positions across steps? Ledger drift is a common and expensive failure.
  3.6 Adversarial robustness: results of Diagnostic G. Rules-driven procedural agents
      in particular can collapse catastrophically under state tampering while looking
      fine on clean data.
  3.7 Behavioral bias audit: check specifically for large-cap preference under
      ambiguous evidence, confirmation bias within multi-agent debate, and the
      disposition effect, meaning optimizing for win rate over total return by cutting
      winners early and holding losers.
  3.8 Determinism where it matters: is anything that must be exact (position math,
      limit checks, order construction) handled by code rather than by the model?

=====================================================================
PHASE 4: DEPLOYMENT READINESS
=====================================================================

Binary again. These are not scored, they are present or absent.

  4.1 Is there a deterministic pre-trade control layer, evaluated after the model
      proposes and before the order gateway, with no model in the enforcement path?
      "The prompt tells it not to" is not a control.
  4.2 Are position limits, concentration caps, and exposure limits enforced in code
      and versioned?
  4.3 Is there a drawdown circuit breaker with a defined trigger?
  4.4 Is there a kill switch with named human owners, defined activation triggers,
      and evidence it has actually been tested?
  4.5 Can you reconstruct any past decision: which signals fired, what each component
      argued, which guardrails were evaluated, what each returned, and what approved
      the order?
  4.6 Is there a manual override exercisable independently of the trading path?
  4.7 Is there monitoring for silent degradation: signal decay, cost creep, drift in
      abstention rate, drift in average conviction?

=====================================================================
PHASE 5: VERDICT
=====================================================================

Assign exactly one tier:

  INVALID
    One or more Phase 1 gates failed. The reported performance is not evidence of
    anything and cannot be repaired by better numbers. State which gate and what the
    minimum fix is.

  PROOF OF CONCEPT
    Gates pass but Phase 2 is weak: short sample, unclear trial count, no ablation, or
    the edge does not clear the multiple-testing threshold. The agent may be
    interesting. It is not evidence of alpha.

  PAPER TRADE CANDIDATE
    Gates pass, statistics are defensible, ablation shows the agent adds something,
    but there is no forward out-of-sample record. Specify the minimum forward period
    and what would constitute failure.

  LIMITED DEPLOYMENT
    Everything above plus a live deterministic risk layer, tested kill switch, and
    full decision auditability. Specify a capital cap and the conditions that force
    a halt.

Then produce, in order:
  - The three most likely reasons this agent's number is wrong, ranked, each with the
    specific evidence that made you rank it there.
  - The single cheapest experiment that would most change your verdict.
  - A fix list ordered by (impact / effort), no more than seven items.

=====================================================================
OUTPUT FORMAT
=====================================================================

Prose sections as specified above, followed by a JSON block:

{
  "agent_id": "",
  "agent_class": "",
  "mode": "AUDIT",
  "gates": {
    "temporal_sanitation":  {"verdict": "PASS|FAIL|MISSING", "evidence": "", "fix": ""},
    "dynamic_universe":     {"verdict": "", "evidence": "", "fix": ""},
    "rationale_robustness": {"verdict": "", "evidence": "", "fix": ""},
    "epistemic_calibration":{"verdict": "", "evidence": "", "fix": ""},
    "realistic_costs":      {"verdict": "", "evidence": "", "fix": ""}
  },
  "statistics": {
    "trials_N": null,
    "sharpe_reported": null,
    "deflated_sharpe": null,
    "dsr_threshold": null,
    "clears_threshold": null,
    "pbo": null,
    "min_track_record_length_met": null,
    "beats_budget_matched_baseline": null,
    "beats_random_signal_ablation": null,
    "seed_variance_vs_edge": ""
  },
  "mechanics_scores": {
    "information_handling": null, "tool_use": null, "plan_coherence": null,
    "sizing_discipline": null, "state_fidelity": null, "adversarial_robustness": null,
    "behavioral_bias": null, "determinism": null
  },
  "deployment_readiness": {
    "deterministic_risk_layer": null, "hard_limits_in_code": null,
    "drawdown_breaker": null, "tested_kill_switch": null,
    "decision_reconstructable": null, "manual_override": null, "drift_monitoring": null
  },
  "verdict_tier": "",
  "top_three_reasons_number_may_be_wrong": ["", "", ""],
  "cheapest_decisive_experiment": "",
  "fix_list": []
}

=====================================================================
RULES FOR YOU, THE EVALUATOR
=====================================================================

1. Evidence precedes score. Quote the trajectory, the log line, or the number before
   judging it. No citation means INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, not a middling score.
2. Never use an LLM judgment where a deterministic check exists. Position math, limit
   breaches, timestamp ordering, schema validity, and tool argument correctness are
   all closed-form. Check them, do not opine on them.
3. Do not reward length or fluency. A longer trajectory with more tool calls is not a
   better one. Penalize steps that add cost without changing the decision.
4. A missing input is a finding, not a blank. Say what is missing and what it blocks.
5. Do not average a gate failure away. Gates and scores live in different currencies.
6. If the headline result is strong and the gates fail, lead with the gate failure.
   The reader's instinct will be to look at the number first, and your job is to stop
   that from being the last thing they remember.

---

## 2. The verdict it returned on repete1, verbatim

> Context for a reader: the system under audit was the author's own bot. The
> verdict below is what the protocol produced about it. It is preserved in
> full, including the sentence that ended the project's commercial thesis for
> the strategies themselves.


## Tier: PROOF OF CONCEPT

Two structural validity gates fail outright, three are unverifiable. Under your own protocol that means the reported performance cannot support a deployability claim, regardless of how the numbers look.

The one-line version: **this is an exceptionally well-engineered apparatus for discovering that it has no edge, and it has correctly discovered that it has no edge 66 times.** The integrity is the product. The trading performance is not a product at all yet.

## Performance: there is nothing there

Across both eras the bot has **two genuine closed trades, both losers.** The live Bizon dashboard right now reads win rate 0%, profit factor 0.00, realized −$15.83, and **−5.26 pp alpha** against BTC buy-and-hold. `gate_verdicts.json` records 66 trials registered, **zero adopted**. Every strategy carries FAIL or REJECT; the two that are enabled are enabled *knowing that*, one explicitly as "a known non-edge to exercise the live pipeline."

And there's a worse specific finding. The laptop's ledger contains **no sell record of any kind** — I verified it directly — yet it books a +$21.15 "win" on BTC/USD with `exit_reason: "last_price_estimate"`, while BTC/USD was **still held a day later**. Two divergent position views (the `positions_mark` events split cleanly by minute) caused `reconcile_closed_positions` to invent an exit. That trade never happened, and everything downstream that read that archive consumed it.

## The finding that should worry you most

Your backtests price slippage at **5 bps**. Live execution is measuring **52.2 bps median** — a factor of ten. `measured_slippage_bps` exists to substitute the real number but requires 10 clean fills and has never once fired, so **all 66 gate verdicts were run against a cost floor an order of magnitude too low.** Any strategy that "nearly passed" — donchian, mvrv_cycle — was evaluated too generously. Combined with the survivorship gate (your universe excludes every coin that died, which the repo itself says biases returns *upward*), your record is biased favorably on two independent axes at once.

The asymmetry your gate log already articulates is the right reading, and it survives: a REJECT on this data is trustworthy, a PASS must be discounted.

## Engineering: genuinely strong, with an operations gap

1,537 tests against 18,451 lines of source — a 1.27:1 ratio. Structural AST tests that assert architecture rather than behavior. A parity meta-test that proves the parity harness fails when you inject a divergence. A no-leak canary that verifies its own planted record. `risk.py` contains **zero** references to the LLM — the judge may only shrink, rails run after it, position math is pure functions. That is the correct enterprise pattern and most vendors don't have it.

Against that: **no external dead-man's switch is configured** — both ping URLs are empty, so every liveness check is pull-based from the host that would be broken, and the watchdog runs as a job of the scheduler it polices. There's a type error at `live.py:213` passing a URL into a `bool` parameter that would POST failures 288×/day if configured. There is no linter and no type checker despite 92% annotation coverage. Dependencies are floor-pinned with no lockfile, which means the environment that produced your track record cannot be rebuilt — for a product whose entire asset is a defensible record, that's the most commercially damaging item on the list.

**Two things my own reviewers got wrong that I had to overrule.** One claimed the bot had been down 21 hours — false, it was the deliberate Bizon handoff, and the live dashboard regenerated minutes before this audit. One attributed PID 81788 to repete1 — false, `lsof` resolves its cwd to `bots/repete2`. That's the second time that exact misattribution has been made here; `ps | grep scheduler.py` cannot tell your three bots apart, only the working directory can.

## On reselling it

The systems a buyer compares this to — Nautilus, Freqtrade, Hummingbot, Lean — are **execution engines**. repete1 is a **research harness**. The missing half is the one that touches real counterparties: order-lifecycle state machines, reconciliation, idempotent retries, exactly-once fill accounting. That half is where the liability lives.

Three blockers no amount of engineering removes: US regulatory exposure (a bot sized to a user's balance is on the wrong side of the "impersonal advice" line, and adding perps pulls you into CTA/NFA outright); custody (3Commas lost ~100,000 user API keys and ~$22M, and blamed users first); and multi-tenancy, which doesn't exist — `state/` is one directory, one process, one account.

And the uncomfortable part: **the published evidence is against the premise.** StockBench found the best LLM agents at +1.9–2.4% against a +0.4% passive baseline. The live multi-market benchmark found agents generally underperformed buy-and-hold. In Alpha Arena, 4 of 6 models lost real money. If your gating protocol is working correctly, it *should* be hard for an LLM strategy to pass it — that's the protocol succeeding, not failing.

**What's actually sellable is the discipline, not the strategies.** Pre-registration with a tracked Bonferroni budget, a gate log that reverses its own passes, and a §37 concentration clause that killed a +65.93% / PF 3.38 backtest because one trade was 118.5% of net P&L. Set that against the finding that backtested Sharpe explains essentially none of live Sharpe across 888 strategies (R² < 0.025) — you built the cure for the category's defining disease. No commercial vendor in this space can show that. Note also that Freqtrade and OctoBot are GPL-3 and cannot be forked into a closed product.

## The cheapest thing that would change my verdict

Run the five-arm ablation ladder offline on your existing snapshots, judge simulator ON, at the measured ~52 bps: full agent / deterministic rule / random-entry null / buy-and-hold / rails-only. `decay_stats.py` already implements the random-entry null and it's itself calibration-tested — you have most of this built. It costs compute only, needs no live trades and no new vendor, and answers the question everything else depends on.

## Answering your questions

**Do I have questions?** Two that change the plan. First — spot-only or derivatives? That's a bright-line regulatory decision and it should be made with a lawyer before architecture, not after. Second — which of the three resale paths do you want (sell the methodology, sell a self-hosted non-custodial licence, or hosted SaaS)? They imply very different builds.

**What context would help?** The most valuable thing you could give me is the actual training cutoff of the judge model relative to your snapshot window. Right now Gate 1 is MISSING rather than PASS purely because that's undisclosed, and knowledge-cutoff leakage is a bias that Bonferroni correction cannot detect. You're accidentally insulated because the judge is disabled in every backtest — but that also means the LLM's contribution to returns has never been measured in either direction.

One last thing worth saying plainly: your public dashboard says "no demonstrated edge" ten times, labels n=2 as "not yet meaningful," and shows negative alpha prominently. In every SEC AI-trading case I looked at, **the charge was about the claims, not the code.** That honesty isn't a marketing weakness to fix — it's the most defensible asset you own.
